title: Comparison of Disinfection Agents on Smallmouth Grunt Eggs
author: Tory Stoddard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.baqxidxn

steps.title: Separate eggs with 40 μm sieve
steps.instruction: Use a 40 μm sieve (siv) to separate eggs from the aerated collection bucket.

steps.title: Transfer eggs to graduated cylinder
steps.instruction: Pipette a few milliliters of the collected eggs from the sieve into a 10 mL graduated cylinder.

steps.title: Prepare iodine disinfectant bath
steps.instruction: Fill a watch glass halfway with filtered seawater, then add iodine at a concentration of 1 mL iodine per 1 L filtered seawater.

steps.title: Prepare filtered seawater rinse bath
steps.instruction: Fill a second watch glass completely with filtered seawater (no iodine).

steps.title: Measure and aliquot 0.3 mL eggs
steps.instruction: Allow the eggs in the graduated cylinder to settle and float to the top, then measure the volume and pipette exactly 0.3 mL of eggs out.

steps.title: Treat eggs with iodine
steps.instruction: Place a 40 μm sieve into the iodine treatment bath, pipette the 0.3 mL of eggs onto the sieve, swirl gently in a circular motion for about 30 seconds to mix, and keep the eggs exposed to iodine for 5 minutes using a timer.

steps.title: Rinse eggs in seawater
steps.instruction: After the 5‑minute iodine exposure, transfer the sieve to the rinse watch glass containing only filtered seawater and swirl gently in a circular motion for about 30 seconds.

steps.title: Distribute eggs into three watch glasses
steps.instruction: Pipette approximately 0.1 mL of eggs from the sieve into each of three watch glasses that already contain filtered seawater.

steps.title: Incubate watch glasses in heated trough
steps.instruction: Place the three watch glasses containing the eggs into the heated trough.

steps.title: Return leftover eggs to bucket
steps.instruction: Pour any leftover eggs back into the original collection bucket to maintain oxygen supply.
